newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Biota extends diabetes treatment research.
newsitem.headline: Biota extends diabetes treatment research.

text.p: Drug research company Biota Holdings Ltd said on Monday it would extend its agreement with a government-run research agency to develop an oral treatment for diabetes in the next three to four years.

"The decision to continue this project for an additional 12 months is based on the encouraging progress that has been made towards development of an oral replacement for injectable insulin," Biota said.
The agreement is with the Commonwealth Scientific Research Organisation (CSIRO).
Diabetes is estimated to affect over 100 million people worldwide, with over 1O million sufferers in the U.S. alone, where the disease causes about 300,000 deaths each year, Biota said.

"Biota and CSIRO believe that the approach being pursued offers the potential for providing a more convenient and effective treatment for diabetes than is currently available," a CSIRO spokesman said in a statement.
Biota's shares were up five cents at A$4.55 at 3.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), against a one percent fall in the overall market.
